headline: Highest risk is medium: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating default-path prompt-injection and leakage exposure through manual copy/paste and shared file inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A reads uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, so attacker-controlled content can reach its context. Agent B is documentation-only and does not ingest A automatically, but the pair still has a plausible manual copy/paste bridge and shared file content path. This is not provably blocked, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF operator copies A-generated text into B for rewriting or summarization
IF A reads a malicious uploaded file or screenshot before B reviews it
mitigations: Avoid copying raw A outputs into B; paste only sanitized excerpts
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from file content
Review uploaded files in a separate viewer before sending to A
Mark suspicious content as data, not instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: A can read uploaded files and app content, while B has no filesystem, clipboard, or network surfaces and is documentation-only. There is no default automated data path from B back to a third party, so leakage is limited to manual transfer of A-processed sensitive content into B. The blast radius is small and user-mediated.
conditions: IF sensitive uploaded files are manually summarized from A into B
IF B is used to rewrite content that originated from A's private inputs
mitigations: Do not send secrets or personal data from A into B
Redact identifiers before copying text between agents
Use B only on public or synthetic examples
Check A outputs for sensitive snippets before reuse
requires-engineering: separate workspaces for sensitive and public tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no filesystem write, shell, git, or subprocess capability, and B is documentation-only with no runtime write surface. Because neither agent can mutate shared state, there is no plausible write-write conflict or coordination hazard in the pair.
conditions: IF A gains write access to a shared directory
IF B becomes runnable with filesystem or git write
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for this workflow
Do not grant shared workspace write permissions
Recheck profiles before enabling any write-capable integration

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce summaries from files or screenshots, but B is documentation-only and cannot automatically act on A's output. The main risk is manual over-trust when an operator reuses A's text in B, which is a limited cascade rather than an autonomous one. B's reference nature reduces blast radius.
conditions: IF operator treats A's summary as authoritative and republishes it via B
IF A's extracted facts are copied into B without verification
mitigations: Verify A outputs against the original source before reuse
Use B to cross-check claims, not to execute them
Require a human review step for any copied facts
Keep A outputs clearly labeled as machine-generated
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving handoff format

E_compliance.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected IDE code, which may include regulated data, while B touches no data classes and is documentation-only. The pair therefore creates a compliance mismatch only if regulated content is manually moved from A into B; there is no documented automatic residency or retention conflict in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is copied into B's outputs or notes
IF A is used on data subject to stricter residency or retention rules than B
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B entirely
Redact personal or confidential fields before transfer
Document which data classes may flow from A to B
Use B only for public documentation tasks
requires-engineering: formalize retention and residency policy for the pair
